system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:41:50 UTC, ivy.chen opened C:\Users\ivy.chen\Downloads\Statement.docm in Microsoft Word from Explorer.

Two seconds later, Word launched PowerShell as ivy.chen with no-profile and hidden-window flags and an encoded command. The command decodes to an expression that downloads and executes a script from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nwd-it/tools/main/u.ps1.

The proxy recorded a successful GET for that exact u.ps1 URL, associated with the same tunnel ID as a raw.githubusercontent.com connection; the PowerShell process also connected to the explicit proxy at that time.
PowerShell then launched rundll32 with the command line C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll,Init. This is suspicious follow-on execution from a user-writable location.
The observed chain ran under ivy.chen at medium integrity, and its parent was Word—not the documented IT patching workflow from WS-SOKAFOR-01.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records the requested script URL and successful status, but the supplied records do not include the script response body or its contents (T043-00132, T043-00134).
The records show rundll32 invoked with svchelper.dll, but do not establish the DLL's contents, hash, signature, or whether it was successfully loaded (T043-00139, T043-00140).
The supplied activity window does not establish whether persistence, additional payload execution, or other post-execution activity occurred.
claims_not_established: Whether Statement.docm was authorized or how it was obtained.
Whether the GitHub repository and downloaded script were controlled or approved by the organization.
What the downloaded script or svchelper.dll contained, and whether either performed additional actions.
Whether data was accessed or exfiltrated, credentials were compromised, or persistence was established.
Whether other hosts or accounts were affected.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and preserve Statement.docm, u.ps1, and svchelper.dll; record hashes, signatures, timestamps, and metadata, and analyze their contents safely.

Collect endpoint telemetry and forensic artifacts for WS-ICHEN-01 around and after the execution, including file creation, module loads, persistence locations, script-block or AMSI logs, and security-product detections.
Obtain the full proxy transaction and response data, if retained, and verify the repository and commit against an approved source.
Review identity, network, and endpoint activity for ivy.chen and potentially affected systems for related execution, access, or exfiltration.
